label: angustiseptate
definition: A flattened quality inhering in a fruit by virtue of its being compressed at right angles to the septum, so that the septum lies across the narrowest diameter of the fruit. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991103 depressed; the counterpart latiseptate (compressed parallel to the septum) would be a sibling.
reason: A standard Brassicaceae fruit character. PATO:0002054 laterally compressed is defined by the body axes, not by the septum.
Ribs, wings or fruit walls thickened with corky tissue. The corky texture is the quality and the thickening is implied.
Without stalked glands = not stipitate-glandular. Negating glandular trichome as a whole would be too broad.
An apex with three minute teeth: a count of 3 teeth on the apex of the bearer, not a quality of its own.
In mosses, alar cells (PO_0030057) abruptly distinct from the adjacent lamina cells: a relation (PATO_0005006 differentiated from) to cells that are only implied, with 'abruptly' as the degree.
Speckled = spotted (rule C334). The paleness belongs to the spots and can be annotated as their colour if needed.
French mutique = muticous, without an awn or point. Same as rule C348.
Sarmenteux = with long, flexible stems that scramble or climb. Same reading as lianescent (C354) and scrambling (C355); restrict to whole plant, stem and branch.

label: pyrophytic
definition: A tolerant to quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its surviving recurrent fire, typically by resprouting from protected underground or basal organs. NOTE: Ecological like FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic; probably outside PATO's scope.
reason: Used consistently for fire-adapted savanna herbs and subshrubs in African floras. No existing term.
Cordlike rhizomes are long, slender and tough. Filiform is the nearest existing term, but a cord is thicker than a thread.
Two shape values joined: cylindrical (PATO_0001873) and funnel-shaped (PATO_0002521).
A seed coat with fine, elongate pits. Foveate carries the quality; the shape of the pits is a detail of the pits.
Semirounded lobes and scars have a half-round outline. The word could also mean 'somewhat rounded', so the mapping is uncertain.
Hairs confined to a tuft is the definition of bearded.
Negates hairs confined to a tuft. Saying 'hairs absent' would be wrong, because other hairs may be present.
Hooded = cucullate. 'Together with the dorsal sepal' is a relation to another part and stays in the record.
Paniculoid = resembling a panicle.
A PO inflorescence type, like 'head' (C262). 'Inflorescence an anthela' names the bearer class.

label: costal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located along or next to the midrib (costa) of the structure that bears it. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991208 marginal; PO_0030072 costa is the moss midrib only.
reason: Costal sori, along the pinna midrib, is a standard fern character. Some examples ('veins forming costal...') are fragments.
Biramous hairs have two arms. The quality belongs to the trichome, not to the stem it is reported on.
sub- + filiform (PATO_0104351), the approximate-value pattern like suborbicular.
Few-flowered is a count of flowers (counted part 'flowered' → flower). The vague count is held as not numeric.
Many-flowered is a count of flowers. The vague count is held as not numeric.

label: sinistrorse
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a corolla or perianth by virtue of its lobes being contorted in bud, each lobe overlapping its neighbour on the left when the bud is viewed from above. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991083 valvate and FLOPO:0991063 imbricate; a dextrorse sibling is needed; usage of the convention varies between authors.
reason: A standard aestivation character (e.g. Apocynaceae). PATO_0002202 left handedness is about which hand is used, not about direction of overlap.
PATO high saturation has 'bright' as a synonym.
Vegetative culms and stems are non-flowering shoots. The word describes which bearer is meant, not a quality.
Applanate = flattened.
Fruit with glochids means glochids are present. The FLOPO_0986043 definition (cactus areoles) needs widening to barbed bristles on Boraginaceae nutlets.
Pencil-like stems and branch tips are slender, terete and rod-like.
sub- + scapiform (almost scape-like). The base value 'scapose' has no term yet, so this waits on that class.
